title: A three-period test has below 5 percent mean power for a 1.7 m/s Wolf 1061 wave with 8 m/s HIRES white noise
abstract: We test power at three fixed Wolf 1061 outer periods in 193 HARPS and 94 HIRES samples. Circular injections use known Gaussian covariance and a 1 percent family null threshold. At 1.7 m/s amplitude, mean HIRES detection power is 3.4 to 4.1 percent with an 8 m/s independent noise term. Mean power to detect and select the correct period is 2.6 to 3.4 percent. With a 2 m/s term, correct detection power rises to 43 to 53 percent. A 30-day correlation control gives lower power. A free trend retains the low-power result. The fixed period shapes have limited overlap. The result does not detect or exclude a planet, resolve full orbit aliases, or identify the noise source. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure and source hashes permit reproduction. External source records are excluded.

display.caption: Power to detect and select the injected period. Lines give phase means; shades give phase ranges. Each fit knows the simulated noise covariance.

citations.reason: Source selection, hashes and retrieval rule; new sensitivity tests address its open noise limit.
